Subject: Production regression after v12 roll (quant int8) - p99 & throughput

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

We pushed Redwood v12 to production this morning (modelpack v12 + int8 quant profile QV2) and immediately started seeing severe regressions: p99 increased ~2.5x and end-to-end throughput dropped ~45%. This is impacting our core auth flow (latency-sensitive). Attached is a quick p95/p99 export and a short sampling of errors.

Immediate asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the v12 quant path changed kernel selection for small-sequence traffic?
- We need a rollback or mitigation window today — this is customer-facing and leadership is already involved.

Attachments: p95_report_20260914.csv

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Production regression after v12 roll (quant int8) - p99 & throughput

Kimberly / Alex — quick findings from an initial pass against HelixGuard traces (thanks for the p95 export):
- The QV2 profile triggers an int8 fastpath for certain attention kernels. For short-sequence traffic (median 28 tokens) we see a switch from our optimized fused kernel to a fallback path that increases per-token GPU time (observed +30–45% kernel latency).
- We also observed increased KV cache churn on requests that do few repeats; caching heuristics misaligned with HelixGuard's short sequences.

Immediate mitigations we can do now:
- Emergency rollback of quant profile to the previous qfp (QV1) which will restore the fused kernel selection. Estimated customer-impact window: 12–18 minutes (coord required for modelwarm).
- If rollback is not acceptable, we can force the fused kernel selection for v12 for the affected traffic class (hotfix) — estimated 30–45 min operation with lower risk of cache cold-starts.

I uploaded server logs and a short kernel trace bundle into the ticket. Action items:
- Alex: please share server-logs-20260914.tar.gz (if you have the edge-box logs) and confirm which canonical endpoints to target for rollback.
- Kimberly / Marissa: recommend prioritizing a rollback to restore SLOs while we root-cause.

—Aditya

Subject: Re: Production regression after v12 roll (quant int8) - rollback confirmed

Alex — quick update after the bridge this morning: we executed a rollback of the QV2 profile to QV1 at 08:40 PT for the affected shard. Early signals: p99 is back within 5% of baseline and throughput recovered to ~95% of previous levels. Full postmortem with timelines and recommended kernel-heuristic fixes will be shared by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments included: server-logs-20260914.tar.gz (support bundle), rollback_plan_v12.pdf (ops steps).

We will follow up with a proposed plan to reintroduce QV2 after targeted kernel optimizations and cache-heuristic tuning. Thanks for the quick coordination — we know this was disruptive and will prioritize HelixGuard for the first re-test.

Kimberly Park
